note: Source's 'numerous' in 'late numerous reverses of fortune' is dropped.
replacement: The Lacedaemonians saw the Athenians masters of Cythera and expected landings of the same kind on their coasts. They nowhere opposed them in force, but sent garrisons here and there through the country, each made up of as many heavy infantry as the threatened points seemed to require, and for the most part kept strictly on the defensive. They had suffered a severe and unexpected blow on the island, Pylos and Cythera were occupied, and on every side they saw a war whose rapidity defied precaution. They lived in constant fear of internal revolution, and now took the unusual step of raising four hundred horse and a force of archers. They became more timid than ever in military matters, since they found themselves involved in a naval struggle, which their organization had never contemplated, and against Athenians, who always counted an enterprise left unattempted as a success thrown away. Besides this, their numerous recent reverses, coming one upon another without any reason, had thoroughly unnerved them. They were always afraid of a second disaster like that on the island, and so scarcely dared to take the field. They fancied that they could not make a move without a blunder, for they were new to the experience of adversity and had lost all confidence in themselves.
